1/11 - If: learned doctors read. I read comics. Then: Reading comics makes me a learned doctor.

• **All-Star Batman #6: New Story for All-Star Batman, the first one was pretty good (but hardly high up on the pantheon of Scott Snyder stories). Hopefully he'll focus more on a plot this time around rather than having a completely action based plot (other than flashbacks).

  • Batgirl & the Birds of Prey #6: A bit of an "Are you fucking serious?" reveal of who the new Oracle was in issue #5. I think Barbara Gordon may have the absolute worst luck in the entire DC universe when it comes to keeping her identity secret since the New 52 rolled around. Which is completely and utterly bizarre since her identity as Oracle was one of the hardest secrets to crack in the Pre-Flashpoint universe.

  • Detective Comics #948: Batwoman Begins is the biggest source of anxiety in comics this month for me. James Tynion IV has done such a great job with Batwoman on Detective Comics since Rebirth and he's starting on Batwoman Rebirth as well... but on Batwoman he's paired with Marguerite Bennett (of [Unsolicited Opinions on Israel?] infamy). It'll be great if Tynion can keep a tight rein on her, but if he can't that title is going to stink on ice.

  • Savage Dragon #219: I still enjoy the title, but I can't really recommend it to anyone because of the massive amount of continuity that would be required to catch up. (For example, of the four main characters of the title (Malcolm Dragon, his wife, Malcolm's sort of step-sister Angel, and Savage Dragon, only one of them, Malcolm's wife, is from the universe where the story takes place.)

  • Amazing Spider-man Renew Your Vows #3: While this title hasn't been amazing, it's perfect for me because it's really scratched that itch I had when it came to Peter Parker and Mary Jane.

  • Daredevil #15: So last week I drove around town for about 3 hours looking for the last issue of Daredevil I needed (#345 if anyone cares) and I finally found it. So now I can finally start reading them through. I'm only up to #90 right now (started at #81 because that was the first issue where Black Widow started to co-star), but I figure I might as well subscribe and stay caught up on the regular series.

  • Silk #16: I finalized the decision that issue #17 (the last Clone Conspiracy tie-in) is going to be my last issue of this. It just doesn't grab me the way it used to when the character was still fresh.

  • Spider-man/Deadpool #13: You mean the regular artist and writer are back? You mean for the 4th time in 8 issues, the story that began in issue #1 will actually progress again? Amazing!
